clue.text: Relative turns on electronic organ

indicators.note: turns tells us the word for the relative is read backwards here

parts.note: a son is a relative
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A family member flips the switch on an electronic keyboard instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the son; 'on' places E after it. 'organ' looks musical but is the body part on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The smelling apparatus on the face is a sense organ of the body.

clue.text: Paul isn't prepared for marriage

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, put into a new form, so the letters of Paul isn't are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paul is not ready to get married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges PAULISNT, the letters of 'Paul isn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal word for a wedding, the ceremony of marriage.

clue.text: Game's first shot golfer hooked round edge of rough

indicators.note: hooked round describes the golfer's name curling about another letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros, the Spanish golfer, is known simply as Seve

indicators.note: the edge of rough is its first letter

explanation.surface: A golfer hooks the opening drive around the edge of the rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooked round' puts R, the 'edge of rough', inside SEVE, the famous Spanish golfer. The golf terms suggest a tee shot, but the definition is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the opening stroke of each point is called the serve.

clue.text: Fair means of circulation?

parts.note: read not as honest money flow but as a fairground ride that carries people round and round

explanation.surface: A question about honest ways of circulating money or ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' is the funfair, not just; 'circulation' is literally going round in a circle, as a Ferris wheel does.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ferris wheel at a funfair carries riders around in a vertical circle.

clue.text: Procedure doctor leaves on tongue disease

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the doctor's letters are removed from the word for procedure

parts.note: a drill is a set routine or procedure
a ness is a headland, a tongue of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A doctor walks out mid-procedure on someone with a tongue disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes DR out of DRILL to leave ILL; 'on' puts it above NESS in this down clue. 'tongue' is the geographical sense, a spit of land, as in Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness is a sickness or ailment, a state of being unwell.

clue.text: Sitting target

parts.note: not an easy mark but a prank object that is aimed at whoever sits down on it

explanation.walkthrough: A 'sitting target' normally means an easy victim; here it is literally something a person sits on, which then makes a rude noise.
explanation.definitionFit: This rubber prank bladder makes a farting noise when an unsuspecting person sits on it.

clue.text: Half of omelette swallowed — quite bad manners

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so one piece holds the other
half of omelette is its second four letters here
bad signals the letters of quite are messed up

explanation.surface: Gulping down half an omelette is rather poor table manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of omelette' is its back half; 'bad' rearranges QUITE to IQUET, which is 'swallowed' by that half, split as ET...TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour and social conventions.

clue.text: Pine needle's head found in chunk of wood

indicators.note: found in means the needle's head sits inside the chunk of wood

parts.note: a log is a chunk of wood

indicators.note: the head of needle's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pine needle's tip is discovered stuck in a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' and 'needle' paint a tree, but 'Pine' is the verb, to yearn. 'found in' puts N inside LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to yearn or ache for it.

clue.text: Caught inside, pet can smell of cooking — like the cat that's got the cream

definitions.text: like the cat that's got the cream

indicators.note: inside means the letter for caught is placed within the rearranged letters
cooking means concocting or mixing, so the preceding letters are reworked

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Stuck indoors, a pet can smell the kitchen and looks smug like a cat with cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of cooking' looks like a smell's description, but 'cooking' rearranges PETCANSMELLOF; 'inside' places C within the result. Note 'of' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat that has got the cream is smugly pleased with itself, which is self-satisfied smugness.

clue.text: Go round head of Bangladeshi adult? It might

definitions.text: Go round head of Bangladeshi adult? It might

indicators.note: round means the word for go is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in 'your go'

indicators.note: the head of Bangladeshi is its first letter

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A headdress could wrap around the head of a grown-up from Bangladesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts B, the 'head of Bangladeshi', and A for adult inside TURN; the whole clue then describes the headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapped cloth headdress worn by Sikh and Muslim men winds around the wearer's head.

clue.text: Train MOT people to redevelop and fix back of Subaru — it should take no effort to make it work

definitions.text: it should take no effort to make it work

indicators.note: redevelop means to rebuild in a new form, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged
fix means attach, so the last letter of Subaru is fixed inside the rearranged letters
the back of Subaru is its last letter

explanation.surface: A garage instruction: get MOT inspectors trained and repair the rear of a Subaru so it runs effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to redevelop' rearranges TRAINMOTPEOPLE; 'fix' inserts U, the 'back of Subaru'. The car words point at an MOT, Britain's annual roadworthiness test, but MOT is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A perpetual motion machine is the impossible device that would keep running with no energy input.

clue.text: Fine novel by female, talented beyond words

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of fine are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: able means talented, skilled

explanation.surface: A fine novel written by a woman, impressive beyond description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but rearranges FINE into INEF; 'by' puts F and ABLE beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ineffable is too great to be expressed or described in speech.

clue.text: Almost round fruit

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for round loses its last letter

parts.note: plump means round, chubby

explanation.surface: A fruit that is nearly spherical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last P off PLUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a stone fruit with smooth purple or yellow skin.

clue.text: Bad information

explanation.surface: Bad information.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyphenated it is an adjective meaning mean or dishonourable; as one word it is slang for the inside facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-down trick is a mean, despicable one, and getting the lowdown means getting the inside facts or details.

clue.text: Hammered — as an engine might be?

explanation.surface: Drunk, like a lubricated motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' suggests metalwork near an engine, but it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoroughly drunk is described as well-lubricated, and a properly greased motor has plenty of lubricant in it.

clue.text: Tailor has the sleeve

indicators.note: to tailor is to alter or adapt, so the letters of has the are reworked

explanation.surface: A tailor holds the sleeve of a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like a person but is the anagram verb, rearranging HASTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover or case, just as a sleeve encloses something.

clue.text: Beats up least wild teenagers finally

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of up least are thrown into disorder
finally picks the last letter of teenagers

explanation.surface: A youngster beats up the least unruly teenagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beats up' reads as an assault, but 'Beats' is the definition and 'up' is fodder: 'wild' rearranges UPLEAST into PULSATE, then S from 'teenagers finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that throbs rhythmically is said to pulse or throb, as a drum does.

clue.text: Expensive smack at college

parts.note: a slap is a smack
up means at university, as in being up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A costly blow handed out at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' is the British idiom for being in residence at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, costly feast.

clue.text: Pepper pot I smashed when entertaining chaps

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding guests within, so one piece holds another
smashed means broken up, so the letters of pot I are rearranged

parts.note: men are chaps

explanation.surface: A pepper pot I broke while having some guys round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges 'pot I' into PITO, and 'when entertaining' has those letters host the chaps inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimento is a sweet red capsicum, the kind of pepper used to stuff olives.

clue.text: Our struggles with drainage channel when stuffed with bit of loo roll

indicators.note: stuffed with means filled, so a letter goes inside the combined letters
struggles suggests writhing about, so the letters of our are rearranged

parts.note: an eau is a drainage channel in the English Fens

indicators.note: a bit of loo is its first letter

explanation.surface: We battle a blocked drain clogged with a piece of toilet roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' rearranges OUR to ROU, followed by EAU, a Fenland drain; 'stuffed with' slips in L from 'bit of loo'. A rouleau is a roll of coins in paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rouleau is a cylindrical packet of coins wrapped in paper, a roll.

clue.text: Budget speech needs no introduction

indicators.note: needs no introduction means the opening letter is dropped from the word for speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A Budget speech is so famous it doesn't need introducing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Budget is the British Chancellor's annual financial statement, but here 'Budget' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To budget something is to allocate it carefully in limited amounts.

clue.text: A place to settle United States Of America?

indicators.note: United means joined together, so the words States Of America are run together and the answer read off across them

explanation.surface: A question whether America is a good country to settle down in.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'United States Of America' look like the country; run the words together and the answer spans the end of States, all of Of and the start of America.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is a place where people settle down to relax.

clue.text: No marriage is perfect?

parts.note: a match is a marriage
less means without, none

explanation.surface: A question whether any marriage can be flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: Without a match there is no equal, so 'No marriage' reads as matchless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something matchless has no equal, being unrivalled.

clue.text: Pick hat up before end of sale

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells us the word for hat reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: end of sale is its last letter

explanation.surface: Choose a hat before the sale is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TILE, old slang for a hat, upwards in this down clue to ELIT; 'before' puts it ahead of the last letter of sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of the bunch is the best, the select group.

clue.text: Ordinary effort fails to complete work

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: fails to complete means the word for effort loses its last letter

parts.note: a push is an effort

explanation.surface: Ordinary effort doesn't finish the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to complete' cuts the H from PUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is an artistic composition, especially a numbered musical piece.

clue.text: One's apt goal — to initially investigate end of fossil, possibly

definitions.text: One's apt goal — to initially investigate end of fossil, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the preceding letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the 's is read here as an S, giving ONES

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of investigate
the end of fossil is its last letter

explanation.surface: A scientist whose aim is to begin examining the tail of a fossil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONESAPTGOALTO plus I ('initially investigate') and L ('end of fossil'); the whole clue describes the fossil-hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil scientist studies ancient remains, aiming to investigate them.

clue.text: Small number rioting?

parts.note: an edition is a number or issue of a magazine

explanation.surface: Only a few people in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is an issue of a periodical, not a count.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is conduct or speech inciting rebellion against authority, which rioting can be.

clue.text: Beginnings of poker exhibitions generate surprisingly small stakes

indicators.note: beginnings of picks the first letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: Poker displays surprisingly produce low betting stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stakes' looks like gambling bets after 'poker', but means small wooden posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent pegs are small pointed stakes hammered into the ground.
